messages:
Jason: Heads-up 10am sync with SparkBench tomorrow. They want a performance run: target 150 QPS sustained, 600 QPS short bursts (45s). Need us to confirm test windows, security constraints, and a ballpark cost delta for bursts.

Priya: I can run it. Proposed test plan: ramp 0150 QPS over 4m, soak 20m at 150, bursts = 4x45s @600 QPS with 90s recovery. Model: gpt-medium-8k (quantized, kv cache enabled). Region: us-west-2. Will need either VPC peering or Private Endpoint to avoid public egress.

Lisa: Security checks: customer requires KMS-backed key control, SOC2 report, and confirmation that model weights don't leave their VPC. We should offer Dedicated with private networking for POC. Also need IPs for their firewall allowlist.

Omar: Commercial question from the AE: how much extra for bursts if customer wants them guaranteed? Also want a quick compare: bursts on top of Dedicated commit vs on-demand hosted bursts.

Priya: Quick cost sketch (very rough):
```
base: 4 dGPU nodes @ $4.5/hr = $18/hr
bursts: +4 nodes to hit 600 qps, each burst 45s * 4 bursts = 180s total = 0.05 hr
additional cost ~= 4 nodes * $4.5/node/hr * 0.05 hr = $0.9 per test run
```
Will refine after telemetry.

Jason: Paste that calc into the customer-facing note please. They'll want numbers in the meeting. Also list acceptance criteria.

Priya: Acceptance criteria proposed by AE: p95 < 250ms at 150 QPS, p99 < 600ms, errors <0.1%. If we miss, we'll propose fallbacks.

Lisa: Ops notes: to hit burst targets we'll need pre-warm nodes and shorter autoscale cooldowns. Recommend pre-warm +2 nodes 30s before each burst and reduce cooldown from 2m to 30s for the POC.

benchbot: scheduled job created: job_id=sb-2026-04-02-09

Priya: Test dataset: 12k prompts, avg length 320, 95th length 900. Using continuous batching + prefix caching. I'll seed with customer prompt corpus. Run commands & config will be posted after run.

benchbot: run-start job_id=sb-2026-04-02-09 step=ramp ts=4961234568

benchbot: run-complete job_id=sb-2026-04-02-09 summary:
- soak (150 qps): p50=65ms p95=238ms p99=540ms errors=0.02% throughput=150 qps
- burst windows (600 qps): p50=195ms p95=710ms p99=1300ms errors=0.45% \u2014 p95/p99 slightly over targets during first 12s of each burst
results artefact: s3://redwood-runs/sb-2026-04-02-09/results.csv

Priya: Quick analysis: soak looked clean. Tail blowups during bursts correlate with KV cache warmup and autoscale lag. Each burst saw a warm period ~820s where latencies rose.

Lisa: Ops action items for next run: 1) implement pre-warm +2 nodes 30s before bursts; 2) reduce scale-down cooldown to 30s; 3) increase prefix cache prefetch TTL for the customer prompt set.

Omar: I'll capture commercial implications: guaranteed burst capacity changes the margin. If they want contractual burst guarantees we'll price in reserved burst capacity (adds to commit) vs on-demand per-minute charge. Need a short writeup with two options.

Jason: Good. Priya, can you prepare a 1-page results note + refined cost delta (committed burst vs on-demand) and attach security questionnaire answers? Meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT.

Priya: On it 1 will post the writeup, exact run commands, refined numbers, and the security attachments by EOD today.

Lisa: I'll also send the SOC2 excerpt and KMS/HSM notes to Elaine (customer security).

Jason: Thanks team. We'll use the writeup in the customer call. :thumbsup:
